analysis:
Examined the docs/reference/configuration.md excerpt, the new ClusterPairUpdateProgress.swift, the ClusterServiceWire.swift field addition (head line 77), and ClusterOnboardingFlow.oneBuild. No concrete security regression found.

ClusterPairUpdateProgress is a plain Codable status value. Its Phase decoder maps unknown strings to .checking, which is never ready, so it fails safe. It has no execution or authorization semantics. `target`, `detail`, `request` and `running` are free strings from the peer Mac; they flow into `line`, used for logs and `darkbloom update`. A paired peer is authenticated by the keyed link control session, so this is not an adversary-controlled channel. The remaining question is whether the consumer sanitizes these strings for terminal escapes, and that consumer is not in the supplied evidence.

The new optional `pairUpdate` field in ClusterServiceStatus is backward-compatible (nil default). It carries no secrets and no coordinator or consumer data. It does not touch the TB-002 provider/coordinator wire, A-001 prompts, or the attestation/App Attest authorization (TB-011, A-016).

OneBuild is a pure predicate that returns false when any member's digest is missing or the digests differ. It fails closed and gates replanning only. The configuration.md excerpt is documentation of the cluster console (redaction, owner-only export, confirmation dwell). The DARKBLOOM_NO_UPDATE_CHECK change (visible only in the patch excerpt, not as a numbered unit) adds a reference to ClusterServiceCommand.supervisorConfiguration.

Not reviewed because it is outside the supplied units: ClusterPairUpdate itself, which downloads, verifies, stages and installs a release, so artifact verification and signature checks are not assessed. Also outside the supplied units: ClusterServiceCommand, the `darkbloom update` handling, and the coordinator release check. Those need review in the integration pass, relating to T-043 and A-011, since this PR appears to introduce coordinated auto-update across the pair.
